record_notes.DCP-LETT-2101: June 3, supplied 1857, all six blocks, notes/bibliography and original quarter-mile MathML read. Missing Hooker letter challenges abnormal-development/variability law; Darwin admits botanical counterevidence, difficult measurement and uncertainty, requests permission to state Hooker verdict. Wollaston female-head example in P1 is absent from surviving incomplete 2030 body, despite editorial cross-reference; no full-text knowledge edge from that inference. P2 15 of 16 meadow kinds germinated then dying, weed patch 357 emerged/277 killed chiefly slugs by June 1, not later 62 survivors. Moor Park enclosed/unfenced contrast, tens of thousands and 26-year age are Darwin observations/estimates. ¼ mile not 14 miles. Himalayan-thistle abstract and Edwardsia pod still requested. Worker proposed 2101→2092 joins two Darwin outgoing letters, reject.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2102: June 5, supplied 1857, eight blocks and all notes/bibliography read. Acknowledges missing Hooker letters about medals and botany. Prefers early-career encouragement, explicit special claims and warns general merit could favor wealth/power; hypothetical minister scenario not actual nomination. Supports Lindley, asks Lyell assessment of Prestwich, considers Sedgwick but not Royal same year as Lyell Copley. Later medal outcomes apparatus only. P3 attributes variability rule to Waterhouse, asks test starting from variable organs rather than abnormal development, excludes whole-group variation as potentially different. P4 Equus ancestor colouring inference by analogy with pigeon crosses, speculative vision rather than observed ancient animal. P8 reassurance about private Sharpey letter, not newly preserved incoming wording.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2112: June 25 at Moor Park, supplied 1857, four blocks and both notes read. Encloses seedling gorse, post-cotyledon clover-like leaves tentatively and feebly analogous to animal embryos, asks opinion at future meeting. Editorial summary states broader conclusion more firmly than body. Etty improving slowly, pulse improved, planned return June 30; neither clinical efficacy proof nor completed return. 2114 explicitly answers this embryonic-furze communication.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2114: Incomplete single long surviving block, header Saturday June 28/57 corrected editorially to Saturday June 27. Calendar correction preserves original 28 dateline, not silent overwrite. Body thanks embryonic furze, compares young acacia/Eucalyptus/barberry leaves, notes cotyledon divergence within families and tentatively compares to placenta/amnios. George Henslow letter received two days earlier, but ending breaks at that he writes to say; its religious content missing, cannot reconstruct from Darwin July 1. Darwin separate pencil question about seed shape and portfolio marking undated. Full notes and annotations read. Reverse answer to 2112 and direct prompt for 2116 P2–3.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2116: July 1, supplied 1857, five blocks and all notes read. Visit offer and George Henslow religion concern may belong to lost portion of 2114 or another note; unpreserved prompt wording excluded. P2–3 explicitly answer embryonic-leaf/cotyledon discussion, seed shape/environment speculation and insect larva analogy, acknowledging ignorance. P4 reports Gray tree statistics 95 of 132 (.72), exactly matching 2098 June 1; known by July 1, no exact arrival. Emma/children away, later return dates in diary apparatus not already completed July 1.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2117: July 5, supplied 1857, seven blocks and full apparatus/bibliography read. Asks whether Wahlenbergia variation alone has unequal inclined anthers; published-source question, no received answer yet. Old Spanish nuts float 75 to over 90 days, one of two planted germinates, fresh nuts sink; not blanket seed viability. Owen paper admired while human-subclass distinction disputed; title-year 1858 journal issue does not override explicit 1857 reading witness. Later Natural selection incorporation not original letter text.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2124: July 14, supplied 1857, eight blocks, excluded Please Read last part soon note, all apparatus/bibliography and actual three-part leaf drawing read. a/B/C show successive scale-leaf forms on twelve-day Lathyrus nissolia, C with lateral stipules; no dimensions, not cotyledon outlines. Cotyledons apparently remain underground, function inference tentative. P3 acknowledges missing reply to July 5 question, P5 agrees about nuts; neither is June 27 surviving prompt. P1–2 related seedling follow-up but no sufficient identification of 2114 as its specific antecedent to make second direct pair. P4 laburnum regular terminal flower separate recollection. Urgent Boreau/Fürnrohr loans, Kippist alternative; July 13 oral Lubbock correction invalidates calculation principle, 2–3 weeks work lost. Preserve despondent self-description in its context, not diagnosis.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2130: August 1, supplied 1857, seven blocks and all notes/bibliography read. Hooker childbirth timing prevents early visit. Historical chloroform report is Darwin personal practice/claim, not modern advice. Henslow visit proposed August 11–15; Kippist has obtained Boreau, Fürnrohr still sought. Tabulating marked varieties by genus size, preliminary importance qualified as far as gone, known error causes. List of British, French, Dutch, US, NZ, Indian and Madeira sources includes works done or doing, not proof all finished. Koch/Russian flora requested, no immediate loan receipt. Missing current Hooker note remains absent.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2134: August 22, supplied 1857, ten blocks, all apparatus/bibliography and six MathML proportions read. Birth safely over reported in missing Hooker note. Asks Schlagintweit address for Elliot skins, not current receipt of consignment. Norman employed carefully but three-week holiday slows work. Branching classification and principle of divergence mentioned, explanation expressly deferred. Only three preliminary tables complete: British 134/1000 vs97/1000; NZ150/1000 vs114/1000; French160/1000 vs105/1000. Raw diag/ramme layout and genus-size thresholds matter; British equal 593 species counts called coincidence. Source labels French author Godron in error, apparatus says Boreau; preserve original with annotation. Alternative exclusion of introduced/protean groups not already applied. Andersson Norwegian horse-colour inquiry contingent on suitability, not sent or answered.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2137: September 6, supplied 1857, seven blocks and apparatus/bibliography read. Requests flora loans and Cybele during Linnean Society closure. Miquel only 46 varieties, negative result retained; later 2157 says47, versions not silently harmonized. Gray close-species marked list contradicts expected pattern; source identity not same as incomplete August 2129 which lacks list, could be separate marked material. September5 clarification letter to Gray already written, not answer received. Assumes Hooker has tabulated India, later corrected. Wild-carrot galls enclosed, orange larvae noted, not identified species.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2140: September 11, supplied 1857, eleven blocks, full dated horse-question enclosure, apparatus/bibliography and three-quarter MathML read. Book box explicitly arrived this morning, but not all books to be tabulated or already read; Norman paid later work plan. Corrects assumption Hooker had tabulated India. Thanks Leopoldina election despite no prior knowledge of society. Gray Lessons now finished; Candolle future. Enclosure September11 asks Andersson dun-horse inheritance, stripes and juvenile coat questions, not answers. Organic perfection relative to competition, conifer pollen/drone bees examples, 2000 males for2–3 queens illustrative. Asks Henslow to check waterfowl at Ransome tank. Mud from several sites February10, dried6¾oz produced537plants over six months; 634 is flattened MathML, not634oz. Not proof those plants actually travelled on birds.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2148: September 30, supplied 1857, nine blocks and all notes/bibliography read. Finds old Hooker scrap with Glover hybrid cases, asks identity/reliability/address; source not preserved as complete incoming note. Only some borrowed floras done, evenings-only Norman work slow; Ledebour useful ranges, future Candolle and fuller Dutch flora planned. Results favorable so far, conditional association not settled universal law. New dining/bedroom building, personal ill health, Lenny improved today but hopes temporary illness; later October6 recovery in diary not already known. Two draft chapters took six months, September29 completion noted later; published forms are distinct.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2156: October 20, supplied1857, thirteen body blocks, empty cdnotes DOM, all footnotes and bibliography read. Full query list referenced as DAR114:222c is absent from preserved HTML: div.cdnotes empty, footnotes11–15 survive without its text. Do not synthesize Adlumia/yak/Linum/Saint-Hilaire questions; footnote14 preserves only separately attributed Linum excerpt, not full sheet. Book return planned after instructions, requests permission to keep Ledebour/Grisebach/Cybele, half-Ledebour completion anticipated (genuine1/2MathML). Candolle/Dutch loans future. Children improvement qualified. Kidney-bean notice sent but Hooker hybrid case not yet examined; Fucus reference requested. Worker recovery follow-up found no complete list, candidate finding only. Later December6 answer must be scoped to actual surviving query evidence.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2157: Friday evening assigned October23,1857, seven blocks and apparatus/bibliography read. Exact-day hold added: footnote asserts Friday preceding SaturdayOctober31 was23, but October30 was Friday immediately preceding31; both23/30 satisfy Friday label. Body Saturday shipment and October31 visit do not independently resolve. Preserve catalogued23, do not silently replace with30. Box sent to Bromley/Erasmus address, Saturday arrival predicted, Monday pickup planned. Ledebour2–4/Grisebach/Cybele retained; completion/return not yet proved. Henslow butterfly gift requested. Hooker visit transport instructions and possible wife/baby visit, no proof occurrence. Miquel47 varieties differs earlier46. Candidate supplement repeats23 rationale without independent date evidence; root does not adopt its certainty.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2170: November 14 with month/year supplied from planned London visit and prior Moor Park stay, six blocks and all apparatus/bibliography read. Remaining books to be sent Tuesday November 17, not already delivered; requests Candolle/Lowe/shell book (body says Hancock, apparatus Hanley), ownership or reading not inferred. Adlumia seeds received, observation future. P3 Coe letter and mixed beans received; distinctive first-generation coat/size change, sowing next year prospective. Source 2165 November 4 supports knowledge by November 14. Coe 2171 acknowledges missing Darwin November 13 thanks, an earlier indirect clue without surviving Darwin body. Medals note expressly burned, prompt missing; Lindley award future November 30, Lyell 1858 outcome later. Reported personal rest benefit not a medical generalization.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2174: November 21, supplied 1857, three blocks, notes and bibliography read. Missing Hooker note reports Harriet Henslow dangerously ill; Darwin writes conditionally if worst happens and remembers Cambridge kindness. Actual death occurred November 20 per later apparatus, but body does not show Darwin knew it on November 21. Requests brief news of Henslow and says he will not trouble him directly. Hooker 2178 P1–2 supplies family report and acknowledges loving words; reverse link supported, forwarding mechanics uncertain.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2178: Wednesday assigned December 2, 1857, seven blocks, annotations and bibliography read. Returned Monday from Hitcham, wife stayed. Henslow grief and family work reported; Harriet peaceful death, no pain last twelve hours. Appreciates Darwin affectionate words. First rough Impatiens monograph: 100 Indian species, few extra-Indian, very local species and little marked variation. Editorial summary overstates endemism and says over 100. Later 1859 claim of excessive variation differs and must not be backdated. Remaining query answers future, others cannot answer. Livingstone cucumber report is attributed reading, not Hooker experiment. Lindley applause refers November 30 event. Darwin pencil crossings undated. Darwin December 4 reply belongs next packet.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2030: Additional incomplete Wollaston source assigned early November 1856, seven surviving blocks, all annotations, notes and bibliography read. Scarites mandible size, reduced Meloe elytra, variable Harpalus wingcase fusion, tentative leaf-insect/Homoptera suggestion, Tarphii spine with no observed variation and possible sexual distinction. Ends wishing Porto Santo Helices alive, not in salt water; November 30 experimental entry does not supply exact receipt. Undated Darwin Q and crossings separate. Female enormous-head example recounted in 2101 is absent from surviving text, so editorial reference alone cannot establish that precise extant content as its source. Retain source-extent gap without a forced knowledge edge.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2098: Additional Gray June 1, 1857 source, all 28 blocks, annotations, notes, bibliography and sixteen MathML fractions read. Darwin May 9 letter arrived last week. Corrects six Carex to three first-head and none second-head; 49 or 50 species in 46 genera, monotypic examples qualified. Seventy-six disjoined species in 34 families do not favor small families. Fresh marked article mailed, actual arrival separate. Twenty-five tree-family rows give 95 of 132 trees with separated sexes, exact distinctive counts reused in 2116. Flattened tables need p/m/d legend and original fractions. Orchid erasure and questions retained. Gray regards introduced-family proportions as chance; future Silliman article uncertain. Watson memoranda return promised, not completed. Darwin 95/132=.72 annotation undated, but July 1 outgoing independently demonstrates knowledge.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2129: Additional incomplete Gray source assigned August 1857, eight blocks, full annotations, notes and bibliography read. Constitutional varieties and hereditary persistence suggest an inherent law, while Gray asks Darwin for an account; not unqualified acceptance of natural selection. Explicit missing section interrupts question. Bud fertilization, future kidney-bean inspection, puzzling Adlumia insect access, most cross-fertilization likely; enclosure posting requested. No marked close-species list survives in body, so do not identify 2137 list as this letter by date/correspondent alone. Darwin chapter labels undated. Adlumia link to 2156 missing query list remains pending, not accepted.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2165: Additional Coe November 4, 1857, four blocks, original opener, annotations and notes read. Combined header looks like 14th because place footnote 1 precedes actual 4th dateline; raw opener explicitly 4th. Quotes Darwin published October 24 notice, then reports black Negro bean rows between white Haricot and brown beans: black much mixed, white few, brown none. Bean enclosures received by 2170. Separate Darwin annotation describes crossed beans, undated and not Coe voice. Quoted Darwin prompt distinguished from gardener report; no new Darwin direct reply without missing November 13 body.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2171: Additional Coe November 14, 1857, nine blocks and note fully read. Acknowledges Darwin favour of the 13th thanking for sample, suggesting earlier available beans but missing Darwin letter text. Four answers: own harvesting precludes mistake; four kinds including runner were only kinds in grounds; beans in same pod not different; dozen pure beans of each kind now enclosed. Samples came from black plant sown June and harvested autumn; several quarts reserved and separate planting next year planned. Do not activate this follow-up in Darwin same-day 2170 without receipt evidence.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2092: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. May 16, supplied month/year, five blocks and apparatus read. New question whether unusually developed organ relative to close species predicts variability; crossbill beak and Himantopus legs examples. Nepenthes is explicitly excluded as whole-genus abnormality, not positive example. Requests plant cases. Dryness versus altitude and De Candolle dwarf/hair explanation hypotheses, Senebier authority; conditional relation of dry endemic regions, not settled findings. Subsequent June 3 response requires its own source review. No preserved specific incoming antecedent identified.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2198: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. Three surviving questions, incomplete undated list assigned June 1857; exact-day hold. All body, dating notes and bibliography read. Bound with separate question list possibly October 20 visit; June inference from May 16/June 3 questions and July 5 chapter completion, not exact dispatch evidence. Marianne/Bonin and Greenland flora queries; Danish man probably Lange remains identification inference, not book receipt. Cnestis/Connaris ovary/albumen/calyx differences prompt within-species variability inquiry. No surviving answers or proof entire list transmitted on single day.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2099: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. June 2, supplied 1857, thirteen blocks, notes and bibliography read. Missing Hooker medal letter concerns Royal versus Copley, Lindley versus Hancock/Prestwich. Darwin no longer on council; do not imply council vote. P2–3 promises Sharpey letter in day or two, P12–13 reports now written within later section, not automatic proof dispatched. Earlier private Sharpey letter publicly read unexpectedly. P5 cork self-corrected to work; concern undervaluing Hancock and confusing cleverness/contribution. P11 rereading corrects his misunderstanding of Hooker relative Huxley/Prestwich ranking; preserve self-correction, not only initial judgment. P8 just-started journey conflicts with May 29 diary noted in apparatus; no silent date repair. Later Lyell medal/Beaufort death remain future.

visual_readings.visual_observation: Three black line outlines labelled (a), (B), (C): first narrow simple taper, second wider upright form with short side projections, third central blade with two prominent lateral stipules. Matches successive Lathyrus seedling scale-leaves in body; not cotyledon drawings, no dimensions or scale.

reading_method: Root independently read complete surviving new source bodies, metadata constraints, exclusions, footnotes, scholarly sections and bibliography. Actual special markup and figures inspected where present. Reused explicit accepted primary readings only after matching source and accepted evidence hashes. Historical decisions and notes are handwritten; validation packages evidence rather than adjudicating it.
